data.reasoning: Both models agree the PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO are safe, containing standard AUR packaging with pinned GitHub sources and SHA256 checksums. The only disagreement stems from an API error (HTTP 400) in the qwen3-235b model when reviewing .gitignore, causing an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek model successfully reviewed .gitignore and found it to be a standard AUR repository gitignore file. No malicious code, suspicious network operations, or injection patterns were detected in any file.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement is purely due to a tool error (API failure) in the qwen3-235b model when reviewing .gitignore, not a substantive difference in security analysis. Both models that successfully reviewed files found them safe.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b model failed to review .gitignore due to HTTP 400 API error, causing inconclusive verdict
learnings: API errors during file review should be handled with retry logic or graceful degradation rather than propagating to the final verdict
When multiple models are used and one encounters a tool error while others succeed, the successful models' verdicts should be weighted appropriately
Tool errors (crashes, timeouts, API failures) should be clearly distinguished from substantive security findings in the verdict calculation
